rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to elute all 10 compounds if possible and map the overall elution window without risking truncation. The wide phi range and moderate gradient time should reveal whether early peaks are unretained, whether late peaks need stronger elution, and where the critical pairs sit.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only available gain is to reduce t_last while keeping the peaks inside the gradient. This narrows the gradient to the observed elution window and shortens tG to test how much run time can be cut before the current worst pair begins to lose resolution.

We already have full resolution, so push for t_last under 10 min by increasing temperature and shortening the gradient while keeping the same successful phi window. This is an efficient stress test of the limiting pair around rows 6–7 to see whether we can gain the remaining time without dropping below R = 1.5.

The pair at rows 6–7 collapsed when both temperature and slope were pushed, so back off both by one step while keeping the same productive window. This should recover that selectivity-limited pair while still keeping the last peak comfortably under 10 minutes.

The limiting pair is highly temperature-sensitive and seems better separated at lower T, while shortening the gradient alone may still keep t_last below 10 min. This run isolates the effect of slope from temperature to see whether we can retain full resolution and remove the time penalty at 40 C.

The critical pair is not fully resolved and appears selectivity-limited, so keep the successful short run conditions but slightly narrow the upper end of the gradient window to change where rows 5–8 elute. This may improve the 6–7 separation without sacrificing the already excellent run time.

Lowering phi1 from 0.65 to 0.60 improved the only subcritical pair, so continue that direction one more step while preserving the short, penalty-free run. This targets a small selectivity change around peaks 6–7 and may push their resolution over 1.5 with only a modest increase in t_last.

We have reached the maximum CRF, so now test whether the run can be made faster while retaining full resolution. Shortening tG at the same window and temperature is the cleanest exploitation step; if the critical 6–7 pair stays above 1.5, this should improve robustness margin on the time side.

At tG 8 and 40 C, lowering phi1 steadily improved the critical 6–7 pair, so test one more decrease in the same direction while keeping the proven gradient length. This checks whether full resolution can be retained with a bit more selectivity margin, even if t_last may move slightly later.

The optimum at 40 C is right on the edge for the critical pair, so a small drop in temperature may increase selectivity and create resolution margin while likely keeping the last peak close to 10 minutes. This probes whether injection 7 can be made more robust without giving up the maximum score.

Injection 7 is optimal but right at the resolution edge for peaks 6–7, so shift the window slightly earlier by lowering phi0 while keeping the successful upper bound, slope, and temperature. This may improve local selectivity among the mid-eluting cluster without materially affecting the already acceptable last peak time.

Lowering phi0 slightly hurt the critical 6–7 pair, so test the opposite direction and shift the window later while keeping the proven optimum framework. This may preserve full resolution and pull the last peak a bit earlier, potentially giving a more robust maximum-score method than injection 7.

With injection 12 we have full resolution and t_last below 10 min, so now test whether a steeper, slightly wider gradient can keep the critical 6–7 pair above 1.5 while shortening the run further. This is a targeted exploitation step around the current best region rather than changing temperature, which previously harmed selectivity.

Injection 12 is currently the best fully resolved method, but the critical pair still sits right at the threshold, so make a small later shift of the window by raising phi0 one step while keeping phi1 and tG fixed. This tests whether we can gain selectivity for peaks 6–7 and perhaps trim t_last a bit further without losing the maximum score.

Since shortening to 6 min broke the critical 6–7 pair and injection 12 is only barely resolved, lengthening tG one step at the same successful window should add resolution margin while staying under the 10 min target or very close to it. This tests whether a more robust fully resolved method exists around the current optimum region.

Among nearby changes, temperature has shown strong selectivity effects, so test whether a modest increase from the current best method can keep all pairs resolved while pulling the last peak earlier and maintaining the maximum score. This directly probes whether injection 12 can be improved in speed without the severe selectivity loss seen at 50 C.

The best methods are around phi0 0.15–0.20 and phi1 0.50–0.55; lowering phi1 improves the critical 6–7 pair but delays the last peak, so compensate by lengthening tG to keep the late compound inside the gradient rather than in the hold. This tests whether a narrower, shallower window can maintain full resolution with t_last still near 10 min.

Temperature changes strongly reshape selectivity in the crowded middle, and we have not yet tested the phi0 0.20/phi1 0.60 window at lower temperature. This run explores whether that slightly wider window plus a cooler setting can recover the 6–7 pair while keeping t_last near the 10 min target.

We have two maximum-score methods, but both are close to the resolution limit, so try a slightly shallower gradient at the successful 0.15–0.60 window where the critical pair improved versus 0.65. This checks whether extra slope margin can yield a more robust fully resolved method while still keeping t_last near 10 minutes.

We have not yet tested whether a small further decrease in temperature from the best 0.20–0.55 window can shift selectivity favorably without the stronger peak crossover seen at 35 C in the 0.15–0.55 case. This is one of the few remaining nearby perturbations that could reveal an equally scoring but more selective alternative to injection 12.

With only a few injections left and two max-score methods already found, use this run to probe one remaining nearby combination that could in principle trade slope and temperature differently from the tested failures. It checks whether the 0.15–0.60 window can stay selective enough at lower temperature even with a shorter run, but the current best remains injection 12.

One remaining untested local combination near the high-performing 0.15–0.60 window is a modest temperature increase, which could in principle shift the mid-cluster selectivity differently from the 0.20–0.55 case. This is a final nearby probe around the proven region, while injection 12 remains the best method if no improvement appears.

With only three injections left and no improvement over the max-score methods, probe one remaining nearby shape: a slightly earlier, slightly shallower version of the 0.15–0.60 window. This checks whether spreading the mid-cluster a bit more can preserve full resolution while keeping the last peak close enough to 10 minutes to match the best score.

Use one of the last two injections on a final unexplored local variant near the successful phi0 0.20 region, pairing the wider upper window with a shallower gradient and modestly higher temperature. This is a last check for a fully resolved method that might still keep t_last near 10 minutes, though injection 12 remains the benchmark.

For the final injection, test the only nearby 40 C combination around the strong 0.10–0.60 and 0.15–0.60 results that has not yet been explored: the shorter tG at the earlier window. It could still retain full resolution while pulling t_last down enough to match the best score, but injection 12 remains the safest best method.
